questions.title: Section break
questions.text: A report needs a **landscape** page for a wide ERD in the middle of portrait pages. What must be inserted before and after that page?

scheme.mark_scheme: B.
scheme.explanation: Only a section break lets part of a document have its own orientation, margins, headers and page numbering.

questions.title: Page break
questions.text: Pressing Enter many times is the best way to start a new chapter on a new page.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: A page break keeps the chapter on a new page even when text above it changes; empty lines move.

questions.title: Fields
questions.text: Select **two** items that can be inserted in a footer as **fields** that update automatically.

scheme.mark_scheme: A and C. One mark each; a mark is lost for each incorrect option selected.

questions.title: Page X of Y
questions.text:
Complete the sentence.

To show *Page 7 of 38* in the footer, the word processor inserts the field [[1]] for the current page number and the field [[2]] for the total number of pages.

scheme.mark_scheme: (1) PAGE (2) NUMPAGES
scheme.explanation: Both are fields, so they update when pages are added or removed.

questions.title: Header and footer tools
questions.text: Match each header/footer tool to its effect.

left.text: Page number format i, ii, iii

right.text: Shows the total number of pages, as in Page 5 of 40
No header on the title page
Roman numerals for the contents pages
A section can have its own header text

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R2, L2–R4, L3–R1, L4–R3. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Link to previous
questions.text: Arman inserted a section break before chapter 4 and changed its header to *4 Testing*. The headers of chapters 1–3 also changed to *4 Testing*. Why?

options.content: He used a page break instead
**Link to Previous** was still switched on

scheme.mark_scheme: B.
scheme.explanation: While a section's header is linked to the previous section, both share the same header. Switch Link to Previous off first.

questions.title: Odd and even pages
questions.text: A project report is printed on both sides and bound like a book. The page numbers must always be on the **outside edge**. Which option is used?

options.content: Page number format i, ii, iii

scheme.mark_scheme: B.
scheme.explanation: Odd (right-hand) pages get the number on the right; even (left-hand) pages on the left.

questions.title: Restarting numbering
questions.text: A document can number its contents pages i, ii, iii and then start chapter 1 at page 1, provided a section break separates them.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.
scheme.explanation: Each section can have its own page-number format and Start at value.

questions.title: Footnote settings
questions.text: Tick (✓) the setting needed for each requirement.

prefill: Each chapter's footnotes should start again from 1
All notes should be moved to the end of the report

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Number format (1); 2 Numbering restart (1); 3 Convert to endnotes (1)
scheme.model_answer: 1 Number format; 2 Numbering restart; 3 Convert to endnotes.

questions.title: Formatting all notes
questions.text: The teacher asks for every footnote in a 60-page report to be 9 pt with single spacing. What is the best way?

options.content: Select each footnote and change its font
Change the Normal style to 9 pt

scheme.mark_scheme: B.
scheme.explanation: Changing the style changes every note at once; changing Normal would also shrink the main text.

questions.title: Number formats of notes
questions.text: If a report uses both footnotes and endnotes, both should be numbered 1, 2, 3 so that the numbering is consistent.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: Use different formats (e.g. 1, 2, 3 and i, ii, iii) so the reader knows which list a reference mark points to.

questions.title: The line above the notes
questions.text: State the name of the short horizontal line that separates the main text from the footnotes at the bottom of the page.

scheme.mark_scheme: note separator

questions.title: Footnote or endnote
questions.text: Tick (✓) the better choice for each note in a project report.

prefill: A short comment the reader needs while reading this page
A list of 25 sources used for the whole report
A note that the test was run on the school Wi-Fi

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Footnote (1); 2 Endnote (1); 3 Footnote (1)
scheme.model_answer: A short comment the reader needs while reading this page — Footnote; A list of 25 sources used for the whole report — Endnote; A note that the test was run on the school Wi-Fi — Footnote.

questions.title: Table tools
questions.text: Match each table tool to its purpose.

right.text: Alternate rows are shaded so they are easy to follow
All tables get the same borders, shading and fonts
Column headings appear at the top of each page of a long table

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R3, L2–R1, L3–R4, L4–R2. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Rows across pages
questions.text: For a test-plan table it is good practice to stop a single row from being split across two pages.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.
scheme.explanation: Untick 'Allow row to break across pages' so a test case is never cut in half.

questions.title: Caption
questions.text: Why should *Table 3 — Test plan* be added with **Insert Caption** instead of being typed?

options.content: The number is updated automatically when tables are added or moved
It converts the table to an image

scheme.mark_scheme: B.
scheme.explanation: Captions are numbered fields; they also feed a list of tables and cross-references.

questions.title: Cross-reference
questions.text: The text says *see Table 4 on page 12*. A new table is added earlier in the report. Which tool keeps this sentence correct?

scheme.mark_scheme: B.
scheme.explanation: A cross-reference is a field linked to the caption; after updating fields it shows the new number and page.

questions.title: Aligning table columns
questions.text: Tick (✓) the most suitable alignment for each column of a data dictionary or price table.

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Left (1); 2 Right / decimal (1); 3 Centre (1)
scheme.model_answer: Description (sentences of text) — Left; Price, e.g. 1 250.50 — Right / decimal; Key (PK / FK) — Centre.
scheme.explanation: Text reads best left-aligned; numbers line up on the decimal point; short codes look tidy centred.

questions.title: Merged cells
questions.text: Merging cells in the middle of a table can stop the rows from being sorted correctly.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.
scheme.explanation: Sorting needs every row to have the same cells; avoid merged cells in tables that will be sorted or exported.

questions.title: Sections, headers and footers
questions.text: Three grade 12 students are formatting the 38-page project report for **Jol**, an app that shows bus routes in Aktobe. The report has a **title page**, four pages of **contents and lists of figures**, and five **chapters**. It will be submitted as a PDF and also printed on both sides and bound.

parts.title: Why sections
parts.text: Explain why the report should be divided into **sections** using section breaks.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- each section can have its own header / footer (e.g. the chapter title) (1)
- its own page-number format / restart numbering, e.g. i, ii for the contents and 1, 2 for the chapters (1)
- its own orientation / margins, e.g. a landscape page for a wide diagram (1)
- a page break cannot do this / a page break only starts a new page (1)
Max 3.

points.criterion: Own orientation / contrast with page break

scheme.model_answer: Section breaks let each part have its own header and footer, so each chapter shows its title; their own page numbering, so the contents pages are i–iv and chapter 1 starts at 1; and their own orientation, so a wide ERD can be on a landscape page. A page break cannot do any of this.

parts.title: The title page
parts.text: Describe how to make sure the **title page** has no header and no page number while the following pages do.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- tick Different first page (for the first section) / put the title page in its own section (1)
- leave the first-page header and footer empty / delete them (1)

points.criterion: Empty header and footer on that page

scheme.model_answer: Open the header, tick Different First Page and leave the first-page header and footer empty; the other pages keep their header and number.

parts.title: Page X of Y
parts.text: The footer must show *Page 7 of 38*. Identify the **field** that produces each number.

scheme.mark_scheme:
1: PAGE (1)
2: NUMPAGES (1)

parts.title: The printed copy
parts.text: Explain how the header and footer settings should be changed for the **printed, bound** copy, and why.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- set Different odd & even pages (1)
- page numbers on the right of odd pages and on the left of even pages / on the outside edge (1)
- so they can be seen when flipping through the bound report / are not hidden in the binding (gutter) (1)
scheme.model_answer: Tick Different Odd & Even Pages and place the page number on the right of odd pages and on the left of even pages, so the numbers are on the outside edge and are not lost in the binding when the reader flips the pages.

parts.title: Headers that all changed
parts.text: A student typed *4 Results* into the header of chapter 4, and the headers of chapters 1 to 3 changed to *4 Results* too. Explain why this happened and how to correct it.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- the header of chapter 4 was still linked to the previous section / Link to Previous was on (1)
- switch off Link to Previous in chapter 4 (after a section break), then retype the headers of chapters 1–3 / chapter 4 (1)
scheme.model_answer: Chapter 4's header was linked to the previous section, so they shared one header. Switch off Link to Previous in chapter 4, then correct the earlier headers.

questions.title: Footnotes and endnotes
questions.text: The Jol report uses **footnotes** for short comments and **endnotes** for the list of sources. The teacher gives these formatting requirements.

parts.title: Choosing the setting
parts.text: Tick (✓) the setting in the *Footnote and Endnote* dialog that meets each requirement.

prefill: Footnotes start again from 1 in every chapter
Endnotes are numbered i, ii, iii
All footnotes in chapter 5 are moved to the end of the document

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Numbering: restart each section (1); 2 Number format (1); 3 Convert (1)

parts.title: Different number formats
parts.text: Explain why the footnotes and the endnotes should use **different number formats**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- so the reader can tell whether a reference mark refers to a footnote or an endnote (1)
- with the same format, e.g. two different notes marked 3, the reference would be ambiguous / the reader looks in the wrong place (1)
scheme.model_answer: With different formats, e.g. 1, 2, 3 for footnotes and i, ii, iii for endnotes, the reader knows at once where to look; with the same format a mark 3 could mean either note.

parts.title: Formatting all notes
parts.text: Describe the best way to make **all** footnotes 9 pt with single line spacing.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- modify the Footnote Text style (1)
- set 9 pt and single spacing once, so every footnote updates automatically / consistently (1)
scheme.model_answer: Modify the Footnote Text style to 9 pt and single spacing; every footnote uses that style, so they all change at once.

parts.title: Footnote vs endnote
parts.text: Give **one** advantage of a footnote and **one** advantage of an endnote for this report.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- footnote: on the same page as its reference, so the reader does not need to turn pages (1)
- endnote: all notes together at the end / pages stay uncluttered / suits a long list of sources (1)
scheme.model_answer: A footnote can be read without leaving the page; endnotes keep all sources together at the end, so the pages are not cluttered.

parts.title: Separator
parts.text: State the name of the line that separates the main text from the footnotes.

scheme.mark_scheme: note separator / separator (1)

questions.title: Formatting the data dictionary table
questions.text: The **data dictionary** of Jol is a table of 60 rows with the columns *Field, Type, Size, Key, Validation, Description, Example*. It continues over four pages and is too wide for a portrait page. Other chapters refer to it as *Table 4*.

parts.title: Readable over four pages
parts.text: Describe **two** table formatting features that make this table easier to read over four pages.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Two features, 1 for the feature and 1 for its effect:
- repeat header rows (1) → the column headings appear at the top of every page (1)
- do not allow rows to break across pages (1) → each field's entry stays whole on one page (1)
- table style / shaded, bold header / banded rows (1) → header stands out / rows easy to follow (1)
- alignment (1) → e.g. numbers right-aligned, easy to compare (1)
scheme.model_answer: Set the first row to Repeat Header Rows, so the column names appear at the top of each of the four pages. Untick Allow row to break across pages, so the validation of a field is never split between two pages.

parts.title: A wide table
parts.text: Describe how to show this wide table on **landscape** pages without changing the orientation of the rest of the report.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- insert section breaks (next page) before and after the table (1)
- set landscape orientation for that section only (1)
scheme.model_answer: Insert a next-page section break before and after the table and set only that section to landscape.

parts.title: Caption and cross-reference
parts.text: Explain why *Table 4* should be labelled with a **caption** and referred to with **cross-references**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- a caption is numbered automatically / a field (1)
- a cross-reference is linked to the caption and updates the number / page (1)
- so when tables are added, removed or moved the numbers and references stay correct without retyping (1)
(also: captions allow a list of tables)
scheme.model_answer: Insert Caption numbers the table automatically, and a cross-reference is linked to that caption, so if a new table is added before it, both the label and every 'see Table 4' become 'Table 5' after updating fields, with no retyping.

parts.title: Aligning numbers
parts.text: State how the **Size** column (numbers) should be aligned, and explain why.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- right-aligned / decimal-aligned (1)
- digits of the same place value line up, so values are easy to compare (1)
scheme.model_answer: Right-aligned, so units line up under units and the sizes can be compared at a glance.

parts.title: Merged cells
parts.text: State **one** disadvantage of merging cells in this table.

scheme.mark_scheme: - the table cannot be sorted correctly / is hard to copy into a spreadsheet or database / editing rows becomes difficult (1)
scheme.model_answer: Merged cells stop the rows from being sorted by field name.

questions.title: Reviewing a formatted report
questions.text:
The teacher returns the first draft of the Jol report with these comments:

1. *Page numbers are typed by hand — pages 12–14 show the wrong numbers since you added a page.*
2. *On page 21 the test-plan table continues, but the reader cannot see what the columns are.*
3. *Some notes are typed at the bottom of the page with a small "1"; after editing, a note is now on the wrong page.*

parts.title: Fixing the draft
parts.text: For each comment, name the **word-processing tool** that should be used and explain how it solves the problem.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Comment 1: page-number field / PAGE field in the footer (1); updates automatically when pages are added or removed (1)
Comment 2: repeat header rows (1); headings appear at the top of each page of the table (1)
Comment 3: Insert Footnote (References) (1); numbered automatically and kept on the same page as its reference mark (1)
scheme.model_answer: 1 PAGE field in the footer — renumbers itself. 2 Repeat Header Rows — column names on every page. 3 Insert Footnote — automatic numbering and the note moves with its reference mark.

summary: Formatting project documentation professionally — sections with their own headers, footers and page numbering, different first and odd/even pages, fields; formatting, numbering and placing footnotes and endnotes; and formatting tables with header rows that repeat, merged cells, alignment, borders, captions and cross-references.

blocks.content: In the previous topic you **inserted** headers, footers, footnotes and tables. This lesson is about **formatting** them so that a long project document (20–100 pages, several authors, many versions) looks **consistent**, is **easy to navigate** and **updates itself** when it changes.

A mark that divides a document into **sections**. Each section can have its **own** headers and footers, page-number format, margins and orientation. Types: **Next page** (the new section starts on a new page) and **Continuous** (on the same page).

An **automatic code** in the document that is **replaced by a value and updated** by the word processor — e.g. `PAGE` (page number), `NUMPAGES` (total pages), `DATE`, `FILENAME`, `STYLEREF` (the current chapter heading).

A **named set of formatting** (font, size, colour, spacing, numbering) applied in one click — e.g. *Heading 1*, *Normal*, *Header*, *Footnote Text*, *Caption*. Changing the style changes **all** text that uses it.

blocks.title: Giving a new chapter its own header (Microsoft Word)
items: Click at the start of the chapter → **Layout → Breaks → Section Breaks → Next Page**.
Double-click the header of the new section to open **Header & Footer**.
Switch **off** *Link to Previous* — now this header can be changed without changing earlier ones.
Type or insert the chapter title (or a **STYLEREF "Heading 1"** field so it updates automatically).
In the footer: **Page Number → Format Page Numbers → Start at 1** (and choose 1, 2, 3 or i, ii, iii).
Close the header and check the previous section still has its old header.

blocks.title: Worked example — formatting the Sabaq project report
blocks.content:
A team of three students writes a 42-page report for *Sabaq*, a school timetable app.
1. **Title page** — section 1 with *Different first page*: no header or page number.
2. **Contents and list of figures** — section 2: header "Sabaq — Project report", footer page numbers **i, ii, iii**.
3. **Chapters** — section 3: *Link to previous* off; header = **STYLEREF** field showing the current Heading 1 ("2 Design"); footer "Page **PAGE** of **NUMPAGES**", numbering restarts at **1**.
4. **ERD and Gantt chart** — a short section in **landscape** orientation, with the same header (linked to previous).
5. The **Header** and **Footer** styles are changed once (font 9 pt, grey) — every header in all sections updates.

blocks.title: Manual formatting vs automatic tools
rows: Make text bold and bigger each time
**Heading styles** — also feed the table of contents and STYLEREF
Type a number on every page
**STYLEREF** field, or a section per chapter
Landscape page for a wide table
**Section break** + landscape for that section only

blocks.content:
- Changing the header of chapter 3 and finding that **every** header changed — *Link to previous* was still on.
- Using a **page break** where a **section break** is needed — a page break cannot change the header or orientation.
- Typing page numbers by hand — they are wrong as soon as a page is added.
- Pressing Enter many times to reach the next page instead of inserting a break — the layout moves when text is edited.
- Putting so much in the header (logo, long title, date, authors) that it distracts from the content.

A **footnote** is a note at the **bottom of the page** that is linked to a **reference mark** in the text; an **endnote** is the same kind of note collected at the **end of the document or section**. Both are numbered **automatically** by the word processor.
The short **horizontal line** that separates the main text from the footnotes at the bottom of the page.

blocks.title: Formatting the notes of a whole document at once
items: **References → Footnotes** dialog launcher (the small arrow) opens the *Footnote and Endnote* dialog.
Choose **Location** (bottom of page / end of document) and **Number format**.
Choose **Numbering: Restart each section** if every chapter should start again at 1; click **Apply**.
To change how all notes look, **modify the *Footnote Text* style** (e.g. 9 pt, single spacing) — never format notes one by one.
If needed, **Convert…** all footnotes to endnotes in one step.

blocks.title: Worked example — notes in a test report
blocks.content:
In the *Testing* chapter of the Sabaq report the team uses:
- **Footnotes** (1, 2, 3, restarting in each chapter) for short comments: *"Measured on the school Wi-Fi network."*
- **Endnotes** (i, ii, iii) at the end of the document for all the **sources** they used — so the two kinds of note cannot be confused.
- The *Footnote Text* style is modified to 9 pt Calibri, so every note in all chapters matches.

- Typing a small "1" and the note at the bottom of the page by hand — it does not renumber and moves to the wrong page when text is edited.
- Using the **same number format** for footnotes and endnotes, so reader cannot tell which list a "3" refers to.
- Formatting each note separately instead of modifying the **Footnote Text** style.
- Putting long explanations in footnotes — important information belongs in the main text.
Tables in project documentation (data dictionary, test plan, requirements, Gantt plan) are often **long** and **wide**. Formatting makes them readable on screen and in print.
The **first row of a table** that contains the **column headings**. It can be set to **repeat at the top of every page** when a table continues onto the next page.

A **numbered label** for a table or figure, e.g. *Table 3 — Test plan for the login form*, inserted with **Insert Caption** so the number updates automatically. For tables it is usually placed **above** the table; for figures, **below**.
A **field** that refers to a caption, heading or page, e.g. "see **Table 3** on page **12**", and **updates** when the table is renumbered or moved.

blocks.title: Formatting a long data-dictionary table
items: Select the first row → **Layout → Repeat Header Rows**; make it **bold** and shaded with a **table style**.
Select the whole table → **Table Properties → Row** → untick **Allow row to break across pages**.
Align: text columns **left**, number columns **right**, short codes **centred**.
**AutoFit → AutoFit Window**; if the table is still too wide, put it in a **landscape section**.
**References → Insert Caption** → *Table*, position **Above selected item**.
In the text write "see **Insert Cross-reference** → *Table 4*" instead of typing the number.

blocks.title: Worked example — the Sabaq data dictionary over three pages

blocks.content:
- Typing the column headings again at the top of every page — when rows are added they end up in the middle of the table. Use **Repeat header rows**.
- Typing "Table 3" by hand — after a new table is added all numbers are wrong. Use **captions** and **cross-references**.
- Merging cells in a table that will be **sorted** or converted to a spreadsheet — merged cells break sorting.
- Too many colours and borders: formatting should make the table **easier to read**, not decorate it.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Explain why a section break, not a page break, is needed before the first chapter of a report whose contents pages are numbered i, ii, iii. [2]**
A section break lets the new part have its **own page-number format / restart numbering at 1** (and its own header) (1); a page break only starts a new page, so the numbering format and header would continue from the contents pages (1).

**Q: Describe how to give chapter 3 a different header from chapter 2. [3]**
Insert a **section break (next page)** before chapter 3 (1); in the header of chapter 3 switch off **Link to Previous** (1); type / insert the new header text, e.g. a STYLEREF field for the chapter title (1).

**Q: State two fields that could be used in the footer of a project report. [2]**
Any two: PAGE (page number) (1), NUMPAGES (total pages) (1), DATE, FILENAME, author.

**Q: A report uses both footnotes and endnotes. Explain why they should use different number formats. [2]**
So the reader can tell which list a reference mark refers to (1), e.g. footnotes 1, 2, 3 and endnotes i, ii, iii — otherwise a "2" is ambiguous (1).

**Q: A test-plan table continues over four pages. Describe two formatting features that make it easier to read. [4]**
Repeat header rows (1) so the column headings appear at the top of every page (1). Turn off "allow row to break across pages" (1) so a test case is never split between pages (1). *(Also: caption with number; shading/banded rows; alignment.)*

**Q: Explain one advantage of a cross-reference over typing "see Table 3". [2]**
A cross-reference is a field that **updates automatically** (1) when tables are added, removed or moved, so the reference is always correct (1).

- Answering "use a header" when the question asks **how to make it different** — name *section break* and *Link to Previous*.
- Mixing up **header** (top margin, every page) with **header row** (first row of a table).
- Saying a caption is "a title" without saying it is **numbered automatically**.
- Describing a feature without its **benefit** in a 2-mark "describe/explain" question.
